controls.name: C_S20_operating_points_reproduce
controls.must_fire_because: S20 measured the completeness verifier at prefix lengths 6, 7, 8 and 11 on this key set; those points must come back with the same answer sizes here before a crossover is drawn through them
controls.can_fail_because: any shared prefix length disagrees on mean answer count (the probe counts differ by design -- 40 here against S20's 60 -- so the ANSWER means are what must agree)
controls.null_must_contain: a different key file, prover or verifier would move the answer counts

controls.name: C_rebuild_reaches_the_same_root
controls.must_fire_because: the baseline is "fetch the shard and check it yourself", which is only the alternative if the rebuild reproduces the committed root -- otherwise it is a cheaper computation that proves nothing and the duel is rigged
controls.can_fail_because: the recomputed root differs from the prover's
controls.null_must_contain: a rebuild that lands on a different root, which is what a client would see if the shard were tampered with

controls.name: C_every_proof_verified_true
controls.must_fire_because: A29: counts taken inside a verifier that returned False on its first line would be small, stable and fictional
controls.null_must_contain: a proof failing to verify, which raises SystemExit in the measurement loop

controls.name: C_inversion_present
controls.must_fire_because: S20's inversion must be visible in this sweep: verifier work rising with answer size while the authentication path falls. If they moved together, the sweep is not the regime the crossover is about
controls.can_fail_because: verify work is not monotone up in answer size, or the auth path is not monotone down
controls.null_must_contain: a sweep where both rise, which is what a verifier that only folded the path would give

falsifiers.name: F_no_crossover
falsifiers.can_fail_because: no swept answer size reaches the rebuild cost
falsifiers.null_must_contain: a sweep whose largest answer set costs more to verify than the whole shard costs to rebuild
falsifiers.refutes: this spike: if verifier work never reaches the cost of rebuilding the shard, a range proof is always cheaper to check than to redo and S20's inversion is a curiosity, not an operating constraint
falsifiers.fires_when: no swept answer size reaches the rebuild cost
